vessel.name: Newnew Polar Bear
vessel.association: Finnish investigators state that its anchor caused the Balticconnector damage.

physical_cause.label: anchor_drag
physical_cause.basis: Finnish investigators documented a seabed drag trail leading to the pipeline, recovered an anchor with contact traces, and linked the sequence to the vessel.

intent_assessment.label: not_publicly_established
intent_assessment.basis: The technical cause and vessel association are established in the cited police releases, but those releases do not establish premeditation.

legal_status.label: cross_border_investigation_cooperation_ongoing_in_latest_cited_update
legal_status.basis: The Finnish National Bureau of Investigation said cooperation with Chinese and Hong Kong authorities continued.

timeline.description: Replay anchor for the overnight infrastructure-damage sequence.
Finnish police reported a 1.5-4 metre-wide drag trail leading to the pipeline, an anchor near the damage, and traces indicating pipeline contact.
Finnish police stated that the damage was caused by the Newnew Polar Bear's anchor and that international cooperation continued.

evidence.finding: A broad drag trail led to the pipeline damage point, followed by a narrower trace consistent with the anchor-chain connection.
An anchor recovered near the damage had traces indicating contact with the pipeline.
Investigators correlated the physical evidence with analysed vessel traffic and could not visually confirm both forward anchors aboard Newnew Polar Bear.

sentinel_catalogue.note: Catalogue availability only; no claim that these scenes show the causal sequence.

demo_guidance.safe_summary: Confirmed anchor-drag damage associated with a named vessel; deliberate intent is not established in the cited official record.
cueing_signals: poor or delayed satellite coverage increases uncertainty
demo_guidance.do_not_say: Do not describe the vessel or crew as having deliberately sabotaged the pipeline.
